This document is subjected to rigorous technical review before release. It is revised at regular
intervals, and any modifications and amendments are included in the subsequent chapters.
Although Autel has made its best efforts to keep the document as precise and up-to-date as
possible, Autel does not assume any liability for defects and damage which results from the use of
the information contained herein.
NOTICE
This manual is subject to updates and changes. The latest version is available for
download on Autel official website. Errors and omissions excepted.
Any modifications to the product assembled by Autel may affect the product performance, such as
the user experience, appearance, quality and lifespan. These custom modifications (customization)
include but are not limited to the placement of stickers and SIM cards or the usage of different
colors. Autel is not liable for any damage to, or caused by the customized product if the damage is
caused by this applied customization.
1.5 Safety warnings
The safety messages herein cover situations of which Autel is aware. Autel cannot know, evaluate
or advise you as to all of the possible hazards. You must ensure your personal safety before
performing any service procedure.
1.5.1 General warnings
• Read and follow all warnings and instructions before commissioning the charging station.

• Do not attempt to operate or repair the charging station unless you have electrician
qualifications. Only a qualified electrician is allowed to operate, service, repair, and commission
the charging station.
• Perform a risk assessment before performing any electrical work. The assessment includes:
electrical hazard identification, job analysis, risk control measures.
1.5.2 Power and maintenance
• Disconnect the power supply to the equipment before performing the maintenance. Keep the
power off until the maintenance is fully completed.
• Do not perform the maintenance in wet environments (such as rain or heavy fog).
• Complete the following steps before you perform O&M operations on electrical systems:
inspection and testing procedures, preventive maintenance, and troubleshooting.
1.5.3 Fire and explosion hazards
• Do not use explosive or readily flammable substances near the charging station.
• (Optional) Install a fire alarm system to detect fires at an early stage.
• Refer to the vehicle user manual to check if the vehicle releases hazardous or explosive gas
during charging.
1.5.4 Handling and usage
• Do not operate the charging station if the cabinet, the charging cable, or the connector is
frayed, broken, damaged, or cannot work properly.
• Place the charging cable where it cannot be stepped on, tripped over, driven over, or otherwise
subjected to excessive force or damage. Ensure that the charging cable is correctly stowed
when not in use and that the connector does not touch the ground.
• Do not insert fingers into the charging port.
• Do not leave objects inside the charging port.
• Keep the connector away from heat sources, dirt, and water.
• Keep the charging station away from direct water flow.

• Do not operate the charging station with wet hands.
• Do not put the connector into any liquid.
1.5.5 Compatibility and compliance
• Use this charging station to charge only compatible electric vehicles. Refer to the technical
specifications in this manual and the vehicle manual to check if the vehicle is compatible.
• Use the charging station only under the conditions specified in this manual.
• Do not use adaptors, conversion adapters, or cord extension sets.
• Ensure that the charging cable is not damaged or tangled prior to use.
• Use of the charging station may affect or impair the operation of any medical or implantable
electronic devices, such as an implantable cardiac pacemaker or an implantable cardioverter
defibrillator. Check with your electronic device manufacturer concerning the effects that
charging may have on such electronic devices before using the charging station.
1.5.6 Emergency procedure
• Disconnect the power supply of the charging station immediately in the event of danger or
accident.
• Respond to the emergency by performing operations including but not limited to: emergency
power shutdown and first aid and resuscitation measures.
1.5.7 Personal protection
• Wear PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) such as protective suit, eye protection, musk
protection, cut-resistant gloves, and non-slip safety shoes before commissioning the charging
station.
• Complete relevant training courses before you engage in electrical work. The training content
includes: basic knowledge of electrical safety, practical operation skills, response procedures in
emergency situations.

Handling waste incorrectly can have a negative impact on the environment and human health due
to potentially toxic substances. Discarding the charging station correctly can facilitate the reuse and

• Discard electrical and electronic equipment separately in compliance with the WEEE-
2012/19/EU Directive on waste of electrical and electronic equipment.
• Do not mix the dispose of the charging station with that of household waste.

• Do not operate the charging station if the cabinet, the charging cable, or the connector is
frayed, broken, damaged, or cannot work properly.

subjected to excessive force or damage. Ensure that the charging cable is correctly stowed
when not in use and that the connector does not touch the ground.
• Do not insert fingers into the charging port.
• Do not leave objects inside the charging port.
• Keep the connector away from heat sources, dirt, and water.
• Keep the charging station away from direct water flow.
• Do not operate the charging station with wet hands.
• Do not put the connector into any liquid.

specifications in this manual and the vehicle manual to check if the vehicle is compatible.

• Do not use adaptors, conversion adapters, or cord extension sets.

1.2 Purpose and intended audience
This manual applies to the MaxiCharger DH600 produced by Autel, Intelligent Technology Corp.,
Ltd., (referred to as “Autel” in this manual). The Maxicharger DH600 is intended exclusively for
charging electric vehicles and when installed correctly, can be used by untrained individuals. Follow
this manual to commission and operate the charging station correctly.
Installation, commissioning and maintenance of the charging station can be performed only by a
qualified electrician who has the following capabilities:
• Expertise on general and specific rules regarding safety and incident prevention.
• Comprehensive knowledge of applicable electrical regulations.
• Ability to identify risks and avoid potential hazards.
• Familiarity to the installation and operation instructions described in this document.

1.5.1 General warnings
• Read and follow all warnings and instructions before commissioning the charging station.
• Do not attempt to operate or repair the charging station unless you have electrician

electrical hazard identification, job analysis, risk control measures.

1.5.2 Power and maintenance
• Disconnect the power supply to the equipment before performing the maintenance. Keep the
power off until the maintenance is fully completed.
• Do not perform the maintenance in wet environments (such as rain or heavy fog).
• Complete the following steps before you perform O&M operations on electrical systems:
inspection and testing procedures, preventive maintenance, and troubleshooting.
1.5.3 Fire and explosion hazards
• Do not use explosive or readily flammable substances near the charging station.
• (Optional) Install a fire alarm system to detect fires at an early stage.
• Refer to the vehicle user manual to check if the vehicle releases hazardous or explosive gas
during charging.
1.5.4 Handling and usage
• Do not operate the charging station if the cabinet, the charging cable, or the connector is
frayed, broken, damaged, or cannot work properly.
• Place the charging cable where it cannot be stepped on, tripped over, driven over, or otherwise
subjected to excessive force or damage. Ensure that the charging cable is correctly stowed
when not in use and that the connector does not touch the ground.
• Do not insert fingers into the charging port.
• Do not leave objects inside the charging port.
• Keep the connector away from heat sources, dirt, and water.
• Keep the charging station away from direct water flow.
• Do not operate the charging station with wet hands.
• Do not put the connector into any liquid.
1.5.5 Compatibility and compliance
• Use this charging station to charge only compatible electric vehicles. Refer to the technical
specifications in this manual and the vehicle manual to check if the vehicle is compatible.
• Use the charging station only under the conditions specified in this manual.
• Do not use adaptors, conversion adapters, or cord extension sets.

includes: basic knowledge of electrical safety, practical operation skills, response procedures in
emergency situations.
1.5.8 Disposal instruction

to potentially toxic substances. Discarding the charging station correctly can facilitate the reuse and
recycling of materials and contribute to environmental protection.
• Follow local regulations when you dispose parts, packaging materials, or charging stations.
• Discard electrical and electronic equipment separately in compliance with the WEEE-
2012/19/EU Directive on waste of electrical and electronic equipment.
• Do not mix the dispose of the charging station with that of household waste.

A: Yes, it is normal. There are a few factors should be considered in this situation. Firstly, please verify if the supplied voltage is lower than 230V, as this can affect the charging efficiency. Secondly, the maximum current setting represents the maximum current that the charger can provide. However, the actual charging current may be lower due to the following reasons: 1. Vehicle's maximum accepted current: Some electric vehicles have a maximum accepted current of only 16A. For instance, if you have set the charger to 32A, the actual charging current will be limited to the vehicle's maximum accepted current, which could be 16A in this case. 2. Decreased current as the battery approaches full capacity: As the battery reaches a higher state of charge, factors such as heat generation and charging efficiency may cause the charging current to decrease gradually. This is a common behavior to protect the battery and ensure safe charging. 3. ALM/DLB configuration: If ALM/DLB is enabled and confirgured, it also causes the software to temporarily turn down the current to avoid overloading the entire station.

Q: What is RCD?
A: A "Residual Current Device" (RCD), also known as a "Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter" (GFCI) in some regions, is an electrical safety device designed to protect against the risks of electric shock and electrical fires. It monitors the flow of current between the live and neutral wires in an electrical circuit. If there is an imbalance or leakage of current, which could indicate a fault or a path to ground, the RCD quickly disconnects the circuit, thereby preventing potentially dangerous situations. Key features of a Residual Current Device includes: 1. Sensitivity to Residual Current: RCDs are sensitive to even small differences in current between the live and neutral wires. This allows them to detect leaks or imbalances as low as a few milliamperes. 2. Fast Response: RCDs are designed to trip rapidly when a fault is detected. This quick response time helps minimize the risk of electric shock. 3. Protection Against Electric Shock: RCDs are particularly effective in preventing electric shock situations. For example, if a person accidentally touches a live wire, some of the current may flow through them to the ground. The RCD detects this leakage and immediately cuts off the power, preventing the person from receiving a severe shock. 4. Protection Against Fires: RCDs can also help prevent electrical fires. If there is a fault that causes a current leak, it could lead to overheating and potentially ignite a fire. The RCD's ability to disconnect the circuit prevents this scenario. 5. Different Types: There are different types of RCDs designed for various applications, including those used in homes, industrial settings, and with specific equipment. RCDs are often installed in electrical panels, and they can provide an extra layer of safety for both people and property. They are especially important in environments where electrical equipment is used near water, as water is a good conductor of electricity and increases the risk of electrical faults.

Q: What is MCB?
A: A "Miniature Circuit Breaker" (MCB) is a device used for electrical circuit protection. It is commonly employed in power distribution systems to prevent hazards such as fires or equipment damage caused by overloads and short circuits. MCBs are typically installed in electrical panels and function as automatic switching devices. The primary purpose of an MCB is to detect when the current in a circuit exceeds safe limits and quickly disconnect the circuit. It can assess the current magnitude and time characteristics to determine whether a circuit interruption is needed. MCB devices come with various rated currents and breaking capacities, which are selected based on the requirements of different circuits. When an overload or short circuit occurs in a circuit, the MCB promptly detects the anomaly and automatically trips to interrupt the flow of current. This action helps safeguard wiring, equipment, and individuals from potential dangers arising from circuit faults. In essence, a Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB) is a compact circuit protection device that swiftly interrupts current flow in the event of circuit faults, ensuring the safe operation of the circuit.

Q: Why the DLB charging is not meeting enough power?
A: For Meter checking: 1. Check if the CT wires are connected incorrectly. It could be that the red and black wires are reversed, or the positions of the three phases are reversed. 2. Check if the polarity of the current direction is correct. 3. Verify if the ratio setting of the meter is correct. You can find the ratio setting in the manual for your EastronMeter SDM630MCT. For ALM Networking Offline: To ensure the ALM/DLB mode operate smoothly. 1. First, set the router to 2.4GHz only; do not enable 5GHz. 2. This step is crucial: log into your router administrative settings and disable dynamic IP configuration, using static IP settings instead.This way, the IP addresses of the master charger and sub-chargers will not change constantly. IP changes can also cause ALM Networking disconnections. 3. Disable the router’s DHCP lease renewal, as DHCP lease renewals can also cause sub-chargers' IP changing and disconnection. 4. If the router is stable and exclusively allocates the network to the chargers without sharing it with other household devices, that would be even better. Since the specific model of the router the customer is using is unknown, if they are unsure how to implement the above settings, they can consult the router provider

Q: How to deal with "over-temperature fault" ?
A: If the charger is dispalying over-temperature fault, it is specifically described as "fault_board_temp_over", meaning that a temperature sensor inside the charging station has detected an excessive internal temperature, which may impact the safety and efficiency of charging. Causes: 1. High Temperature: The internal temperature of a certain point in the charging station has exceeded the safe range, triggering protective measures. The temperature thresholds are as follows: When the temperature exceeds 90°C, the charging power is reduced by half (derated to 1/2). When it exceeds 95°C, it is further reduced by half. If the temperature exceeds 100°C, the charging station stops charging to protect the equipment. 2. Possible Reasons: 1) Poor Heat Dissipation: The charging station’s cooling system may not be effectively reducing the temperature, possibly due to a fan failure or inefficient heat dissipation design. High Ambient Temperature: If the surrounding environment is very hot, it could prevent the internal temperature from lowering. 2) Continuous High Workload: Prolonged high-load operation could cause the equipment's temperature to gradually rise. 3) Hardware Fault: There could be an issue with internal components, such as the temperature sensors or control board, leading to abnormal temperature increases. 3. Recovery Methods: 1) Restart the Charging Station: After the temperature returns to normal, try restarting the charging station to see if the error is cleared; 2) Update the firmware of the charger to the newest; 3) Reboot the charger.

Q: What is RCD?
A: A "Residual Current Device" (RCD), also known as a "Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter" (GFCI) in some regions, is an electrical safety device designed to protect against the risks of electric shock and electrical fires. It monitors the flow of current between the live and neutral wires in an electrical circuit. If there is an imbalance or leakage of current, which could indicate a fault or a path to ground, the RCD quickly disconnects the circuit, thereby preventing potentially dangerous situations. Key features of a Residual Current Device includes: 1. Sensitivity to Residual Current: RCDs are sensitive to even small differences in current between the live and neutral wires. This allows them to detect leaks or imbalances as low as a few milliamperes. 2. Fast Response: RCDs are designed to trip rapidly when a fault is detected. This quick response time helps minimize the risk of electric shock. 3. Protection Against Electric Shock: RCDs are particularly effective in preventing electric shock situations. For example, if a person accidentally touches a live wire, some of the current may flow through them to the ground. The RCD detects this leakage and immediately cuts off the power, preventing the person from receiving a severe shock. 4. Protection Against Fires: RCDs can also help prevent electrical fires. If there is a fault that causes a current leak, it could lead to overheating and potentially ignite a fire. The RCD's ability to disconnect the circuit prevents this scenario. 6. Different Types: There are different types of RCDs designed for various applications, including those used in homes, industrial settings, and with specific equipment. RCDs are often installed in electrical panels, and they can provide an extra layer of safety for both people and property. They are especially important in environments where electrical equipment is used near water, as water is a good conductor of electricity and increases the risk of electrical faults.

Q: What is DLB? How do I enable it?
A: DLB stands for Dynamic Load Balancing. It is a technology used in various electrical and power management systems to balance and distribute electrical loads dynamically. Ensure that all the screws are tightened to the correct torque after the wiring is completed, and that there are no loosen screws at the terminal blocks. 3. Ensure there is no copper wire or debris left inside of the charger before switching on the electrical power to the charger.

Q: Is it normal gettting a low power even if I set a maxmum current for the AC Ultra?
A: Yes, it is normal. There are a few factors to be considered in this situation. Firstly, please verify if the supplied voltage is lower than 230V, as this can affect the charging efficiency. Secondly, the maximum current setting represents the maximum current that the charger can provide. However, the actual charging current may be lower due to the following reasons: 1. Vehicle's maximum accepted current: Some electric vehicles have a maximum accepted current of only 16A. For instance, if you have set the charger to 32A, the actual charging current cannot reach 32A because it excceeds the vehicle's maximum accepted current. 2. Decreased current as the battery approaches full capacity: As the battery reaches a higher charging state, factors such as heat generation and charging efficiency may cause the charging current to decrease gradually. This is a common behavior to protect the battery and ensure safe charging. 3. ALM/DLB configuration: If ALM/DLB is enabled and confirgured, the software may temporarily turn down the current to avoid overloading.

Q: What is RCD? | What is RCD?
A: Parameters&Functions | A "Residual Current Device" (RCD), also known as a "Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter" (GFCI) in some regions, is an electrical safety device designed to protect against the risks of electric shock and electrical fires. It monitors the flow of current between the live and neutral wires in an electrical circuit. If there is an imbalance or leakage of current, which could indicate a fault or a path to ground, the RCD quickly disconnects the circuit, thereby preventing potentially dangerous situations. Key features of a Residual Current Device includes: 1. Sensitivity to Residual Current: RCDs are sensitive to even small differences in current between the live and neutral wires. Q: What is MCB? | What is MCB?
A: Parameters&Functions | A "Miniature Circuit Breaker" (MCB) is a device used for electrical circuit protection. It is commonly employed in power distribution systems to prevent hazards such as fires or equipment damage caused by overloads and short circuits. MCBs are typically installed in electrical panels and function as automatic switching devices. The primary purpose of an MCB is to detect when the current in a circuit exceeds safe limits and quickly disconnect the circuit. It can assess the current magnitude and time characteristics to determine whether a circuit interruption is needed. MCB devices come with various rated currents and breaking capacities, which are selected based on the requirements of different circuits. When an overload or short circuit occurs in a circuit, the MCB promptly detects the anomaly and automatically trips to interrupt the flow of current. This action helps safeguard wiring, equipment, and individuals from potential dangers arising from circuit faults. In essence, a Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB) is a compact circuit protection device that swiftly interrupts current flow in the event of circuit faults, ensuring the safe operation of the circuit. | A "Miniature Circuit Breaker" (MCB) is a device used for electrical circuit protection. text:
Q: What do I do if the DLB charging cannot meet its optimal power?
A: Troubleshooting | Perform the following steps to check your meter and DLB/ALM networking configurations: Check the meter: 1. Check if the CT wires are connected incorrectly. It could be that the red and black wires are reversed, or the positions of the three phases are reversed. 2. Check if the polarity of the current direction is correct. 3. Check if the ratio setting of the meter is correct. You can find the ratio setting in the manual for your meter. Check the DLB/ALM networking configurations: 1. First, set the router to 2.4GHz only; do not enable 5GHz. 2. This step is crucial: log into your router administrative settings and disable dynamic IP configuration, using static IP settings instead.This way, the IP addresses of the master charger and sub-chargers will not change constantly. IP changes can also cause DLB/ALM networking disconnections. 3. Disable the router’s DHCP lease renewal, as DHCP lease renewals can also cause sub-chargers' IP changing and disconnection. 4. If the router is stable and exclusively allocates the network to the chargers without sharing it with other household devices, that would be even better. Contact your router provider if you are uncertain of how to configure the settings described above.

Q: How do I resolve a PP fault?
A: Troubleshooting | Normal PP voltage ranges from 2.8 to 11 V. When the PP voltage is greater than 11 V, PP disconnection is reported. Perform the following steps to troubleshoot the issue: 1. Use the multimeter to measure the resistance between PP wire and PE wire. If the resistance is greater than 2000 Ω, the connector is damaged and needs to be replaced. 2. If the resistance value is normal, reconnect the connector and replace its cable if necessary. If the error persists, replace the power board.

text:
Q: What do I do if the Wi-Fi connection is unstable or keeps dropping and reconnecting?
A: Troubleshooting | If your Wi-Fi connection is unstable, try the following steps: 1. Restart the router. 2. Set the router/Wi-Fi to 2.4GHz. The charging station doesn't support 5GHz. 3. Restart the charging station on the app. 4. Power off the charging station and restart it after at least half an hour. 5. Check the hotspot connection on your phone and make sure that the signal is strong. 6. Download logs from the Network Operations Center (NOC) and check the Wi-Fi signal strength. If the Wi-Fi signal is weak, we recommend that you use a Wi-Fi router that is more reliable and has a better signal strength. If your Wi-Fi connection keeps dropping and reconnecting, it may be because you connect your charging station to a 5G Wi-Fi hotspot. In this case, connect your charging station to a 2.4G WiFi hotspot instead. If the issue persists, download logs to check if the signal sensitivity is within the acceptable range. If not, use a network that has a better signal sensitivity instead. Sensitivity: For AC chargers, the WiFi requires an RSSI ≥ -75 dBm, and 4G requires ≥ -90 dBm. Q: Why does my charging station keeps disconnecting from the network?
A: Troubleshooting | Each charging station changes its IP address every 7 days. This is called a DHCP lease renewal. After the IP address of a secondary charging station is changed, the master charging station needs to identify it again, and during this process, the master charger needs to be rebooted. If only one charger frequently disconnects, the problem is probably with the charger itself. If all sub-chargers disconnect simultaneously, it may be an issue with the router and network configuration. Perform the following steps to troubleshoot the issue: 1. Set the router to 2.4GHz only, do not enable 5GHz. 2. Log into your router administrative settings and disable dynamic IP configuration, use static IP settings instead. This way, the IP addresses of the master charger and sub-chargers will not change constantly. 3. Disable the router’s DHCP lease renewal. 4. If the router is stable and exclusively allocates the network to the chargers without sharing it with other household devices, that would be even better. Contact your router provider if you are uncertain of how to configure the settings described above. If the issue remains, you can also provide the router model for us to check.

Q: Why am I not able to upgrade the firmware version of my charging station?
A: Upgrade | This issue may occur because you use a custom firmware version. A custom version means that if the customer has specific requirements not available in the mainstream versions at the time, a custom version is developed separately to meet the requirements. Custom versions cannot be upgraded. If the last two digits of your firmware version are greater than 51, it is very likely a custom version. In this case, you need to contact Autel technical support to remove the custom tag on your firmware version in our system. Then, you can upgrade your firmware to a mainstream version. However, you can continue to use the custom version if all functions are working properly.

Q: Why does my meter sometimes display a negative value?
A: Troubleshooting | In PV Hybrid mode, your smart meter may display a negative value because the electricity generated by your solar hybrid system is greater than your total electricity usage. In this case, a negative reading is normal. However, if your solar hybrid system generates less electricity than your total usage, or you did not use the PV Hybrid mode, a negative meter reading may be caused by faulty wiring or meter configuration errors. Perform the following steps to troubleshoot: 1. Check if the CT wires are connected incorrectly. It could be that the red and black wires are reversed, or the positions of the three phases are reversed. 2. Check if the ratio setting of your meter is correct. You can find the ratio settings in the manual for your Eastron Meter.

Q: What do I do if the charging station is over heated?
A: Troubleshooting | When the temperature sensor inside the charging station detects that the internal temperature exceeds the safe range, protective measures are triggered: When the temperature exceeds 90°C, the charging power is reduced by half. When it exceeds 95°C, it is further reduced by half. If the temperature exceeds 100°C, the charging station stops charging to protect the equipment. You can check the following items to troubleshoot the error: 1. Check the cooling system of the charging station. This includes the fan, vent, and air filter. Check whether the fan is working normally, the vent is not blocked, and the air filter is not clogged by dust. 2. Check the workload of the charging station. Prolonged high-load operation could cause the equipment's temperature to gradually rise. Shut down the high-load operations to lower the temperature. 3. Check whether your charging station is placed in a hot environment. High ambient temperature can also affect the cooling efficiency. In this case, shut down the charging station for a while and improve the heat dissipation measures onsite. 4. Check the hardware. There could be an issue with internal components, such as the temperature sensors or control board, leading to abnormal temperature increases. After the temperature returns to normal, try restarting the charging station to see if the error is cleared. If the problem persists, update the firmware to the latest version and restart the charging station.

Q: What's the difference between the Full Green and Green Priority mode and why does my relay trips in the Full Green mode?
A: Troubleshooting | Charging stations have a minimum charging power requirement that corresponds to a current of 6A. If you're solely relying on solar power and there's insufficient sunlight to reach this current and power level, the relay may trip. We recommend that you use the Full Green mode only when there's abundant sunlight. If the sunlight is insufficient, we recommend using the Green Priority mode.

text: 桩侧部署的话，通用的RAG框架本身对内存和硬盘有要求。比如，常用的rag框架【71k star】， ragflow的配置需求是4核cpu，16g内存，50gdisk，以上RAG自身的技术特点决定了桩侧目前无法满足配置。

text: 日志ifconfig_full.log的内容为adb环境中用命令ifconfig查询得到的结果，用于分析数据拨号问题做参考。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第一部分：module_name.log：模组名称信息，用来判断模组有没有没正确初始化加载，usb有没有断开，如果初始化没加载5G模组，或者USB驱动或者硬件断开导致设备离线，那么应该是看不到这部分信息的。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第二部分：sim_status.log：SIM卡状态信息，用来识别SIM卡有没有被识别，以及结论认定为SIM卡服务商提供的业务出现问题的时候，需要将这部分的SIM卡信息提供给客户，让卡户拿着详细的SIM卡信息信息找卡商去查询业务是否正常。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第三部分：airplane_status.log:飞行模式，当数据业务中断的时候，检查是不是被设置为飞行模式导致设备离线的。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第四部分：network_registration_status.log：蜂窝网络注册的状态是后续数据业务的前提，这部分是用来显示网络具体信息的，包括正常注册网络的信息，以及注册不上网络，从这里也能大致看到原因，比如APN设置参数，网络EMM ESM拒绝码什么的。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第五部分：ps_status.log：设备的PS状态信息，我们设备是物联网设备，只需要使用数据业务，CS业务正常与否我们不关心，但PS是数据正常的前提，如设备注册只有CS域，那我们就能根据network_registration_status.log以及ps_status.log来找到数据传输失败的原因。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

text: 第七部分：ifconfig.log：查询设备的ifconfig信息，用来判断设备有没有正常获得IP地址，以及获得的是不是IPV4类型的地址，因为我们的设备只支持IPV4类型的数据传输。这一步也是设备后续数据传输的基础。

tags.section_path: 蜂窝部分规范化流程 > 日志组成说明：

Main Features of Amazon DC Charger Software:
- Supports OCPP 1.6/2.0.1 for backend communication
- Supports ISO 15118-2 with upgrade path to ISO 15118-20 for V2G
- Multiple charging modes support
- Remote configuration capability
- OTA (Over-The-Air) firmware updates
- Fault protection mechanisms
- Local and remote operation and maintenance

Software Architecture:
- Adopts a modular and layered architecture
- BSP (Board Support Package) and service layers have a reuse rate of over 60%
- Shortens development time and reduces risks by integrating:
  - Certified protocol stacks (OCPP, ISO 15118)
  - Security modules

Network and Communication Interface:
- Communication interface framework uses multi-modal redundancy and high-reliability design
- Supports: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, 4G/5G cellular
- Priority order: Ethernet > Wi-Fi > Cellular network
- Automatic failover between communication channels

Multi-level Security Architecture:
- Application layer security
- Communication layer security (TLS, secure protocols)
- System layer security (access control, encryption)
- Hardware layer security (secure boot, HSM)
- Secure development and testing process

Charger Operation and Maintenance:
- Supports OCPP and ACMP dual-channel communication
- Dual-SIM hot standby for cellular connectivity
- Remote operation and maintenance capabilities
- Local operation and maintenance via mobile phones or PCs
- Fault diagnostics and management

DCx Project Plan follows V-model process:
1. Requirements analysis
2. Architecture design
3. Module design
4. Development
5. Integration testing
6. System testing
7. Certification

充电桩监控运维通信协议
协议版本：ver2.6m
协议版本：ver2.6q
道通科技
2024年3月04日

1  范围
充电桩监控运维通讯协议规定了运维平台和充电桩及充电桩内部智能模块之间的通信物理层、数据链路层、交互流程、报文分类、报文格式和内容的定义。
本协议主要包括两部分内容：
第一部分详细讲述了充电桩与运营平台之间的通信方式、认证鉴权方式和之间的通信消息格式；
第二部分详细阐述充电桩内部网关与单元模块通讯交互细节，为远程监控和故障诊断提供底层信息支持。

2  术语与定义
CCU充电控制单元
用于实现与车辆BMS交换，充电机对车辆的输出控制。
ECU/dECU功率控制单元
用于实现安全充电机的安全保护和功率模块的调整输出。
ACU功率控制单元
用于实现交流桩的安全保护和电流输出。
TCU计费控制单元
用于实现人机交换、充电控制、计量计费和后台通信功能的智能硬件。
OCPP开发充电协议标准
用于实现充电桩与运营管理平台充电业务，包括启停充电，身份鉴权和软件升级等功能业务。
APK人机交互模块
本协议指运行在TCU上的Android应用程序，实现充电桩的人机交互功能。
DTM直流计费管理
指在TCU上独立运行的计费管理功能模块，用于接受UI控制和输出结果到UI，实现计量计费功能，并与ECU,CCU及APK实现通讯交换。
ATM交流计费管理
用于实现交流充电桩充电控制管理和后台通讯交换。
UNIT智能单元模块
能够与网关软件独立通信的功能模块，在本协议中单元模块主要包括CCU、ECU、TMU、APK、DTM和ATM等单元模块或软件功能模块。
GATE监控通讯网关
主要实现运营平台和单元模块之间信息交换和特定功能实现。
注：当单元模块和GATE运行在同一个MCU上，他们之间的通讯不限于本协议标准的规范，只需完成相应的功能即可。
HOST运维平台
指充电桩运维监控管理平台，负责充电桩运行状态的实时监控的系统平台。
UPDATE升级服务
该服务属于DTM单元模块中的一个软件模块，负责整个充电桩系统各个单元模块的软件升级功能。
sECU终端监控模块
终端监控模块是直流充电控制器的组成部分，负责终端运行状态及冷却系统的控制调节，负责与充电主控模块通信并接受其控制。
MxCU矩阵控制模块
矩阵控制模块是直流充电控制器的组成部分，负责功率分配矩阵接触器的控制调节，负责与功率模块通信并接受其控制。

3  标准引用
OCPP1.6(Open Charge Point Protocol1.6)
Open Charge Point Protocol JSON 1.6, OCPP-J 1.6 Specification

4  通信架构

4.1  通信拓扑

4.2  监控网关GATE与运维监控平台HOST之间的通信约定

4.2.2 websocket⼦协议名称
acmp 1.0 (注：Autel  charger manager protocol ⾸字⺟简写)。
acmp 1.1 (注：相比acmp1.0，精简消息格式，减少消息头信息损耗，本文档涉及acmp1.1版本格式描述会标记说明)

4.2.3 认证鉴权
对桩认证与OCPP相同，即HTTP Basic AUTH⽅式，username和password值与OCPP的出⼚时初始值相同。桩对服务器的认证⽅式，采⽤X.509证书认证。

4.2.4 请求消息格式
seq为整数的字符串表示格式，递增，到最⼤值后归零，取值范围为uint64。下同。
若⽆特别说明，payload和PL（acmp1.1）可为空。下同。

4.2.5 响应消息格式
status为响应结果的状态，可取值⻅下表。
| 状态值  | 含义                           | 备注                         |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Accept  | 命令成功执⾏。                     |                                  |
| Reject  | 命令未执⾏                         | 在payload中必须包含reason字 段。 |
| Error   | 命令执⾏过程中出现错误             | 错误信息在payload中说明。        |
| Timeout | 命令执⾏超时。结果通过后续消息获取 | 暂⽆明确使⽤场景。               |
4.3  GATE网关与UNIT单元模块之间的通信约定

4.3.1 通讯过程约定
Gate与Unit之间采用Client/Server的TCP通信方式，
所有协议除特别说明外，采用小端传输模式，即低字节在前，高字节在后。
连接由客户端主动发起，客户端和服务端都有权利断开连接。
客户端需自动维护通信连接状态的有效性，在连接断开后，需自动进行连接尝试，直到连接恢复。
客户端与服务器通信前需进行签到。
所有通信报文中除了设备监控数据（实时数据）不需要应答外，其它报文除特别说明外都采用问答方式，有问必有答。数据发起方发送数据后，5秒内未得到回复按通讯超时处理。
通讯超时后需重发数据（心跳等不影响业务的报文不需重发），默认重发次数为3，连续重发后仍然得不到回应，则认为存在异常，停止重发。

4.3.2 端口及IP地址约定
单元模块Unit作为Tcp客户端，监控网关Gate作为TCP服务端，服务端端口8866；

4.3.2.1 一体机IP地址
为了简化设备的IP地址配置，TCU和单元模块采用内网静态IP,内网IP地址设定如下：
| 节点名称 | IP地址                        | 备注说明                     |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| TCU          | 192.168.33.138 ~   192.168.33.141 | IP的最后一个字节为CAN地址8AH~8EH |
| CCU          | 192.168.33.224 ~   192.168.33.238 | IP的最后一个字节为CAN地址E0H~EEH |
| ECU          | 192.168.33.16                     | IP的最后一个字节为CAN地址10H     |
注：DTM，APK与GATE通讯采用回环地址（127.0.0.1）进行通讯，适用于一体式充电桩
5  关键业务流程说明
5.1 监控网关Gate核心功能

5.1.1 Gate上报网关信息到Host
当Gate收到新的Unit签到时，通过指令[UpGateInof](#_网关信息上传（UpGateInfo）)主动向Host报告当前Gate多连接Unit的所有信息（主要包括单元模块和所有子模块Unit软件、硬件版本的信息及节点ID，后期还会增加其他信息）。同时，Gate也会周期上报网关信息给Host，上报周期可通过Gate网关参数命令进行设置。
![img](.\bmp\B5.1.1.png)

5.1.2 Host下发复位控制命令到Gate
Host可以远程下发复位重启指令[Reboot](#_复位重启（Reboot）)到Gate，控制Gate网关或者包括网关在内的所有的Unit单元模块进行复位重启。Gate收到Reboot指令，首先需要判断是否具备条件复位充电。
注：目前规定只有在非充电状态才能控制单元模块和Gate复位重启。
当控制类型为控制所有单元模块复位时，可采用TCU硬件Reset脚对CCU\ECU进行复位。
注：被指令同时适用于超充系统。

5.1.3 Host拉取Gate宿主设备日志处理
Host通过下发[GetLog](#_拉取日志消息（GetLog）)指令到Gate获取日志文件，Gate网关根据指令中的拉取文件条件，查找并将文件上传至Host文件服务器。
根据拉取文件条件，Gate每次可以上传多个文件。
注：每次拉取文件的时间范围必须在同一天，确保每次拉取的文件数量不会太多。
![img](.\bmp\B5.1.3.png)

5.1.4 Gate主动上报记录数据到Host
当Gate本地存在未上传的记录时，可通过[PushRecord](#_记录数据上传(PushRecord))指令上传记录数据，Gate可以一次上传多条不同类型的记录数据。
记录数据的数据区采用base64格式传输，数据的具体内容根据记录类型进行解析。
记录类型与业务类型对应表

5.1.5 Host设置/获取网关参数到Gate
Gate参数设置有两条指令，一条是设置/获取网关运行参数[RWRunParam](#_设置网关运行参数(SetRunParam))Req，一条是设置网关连接参数RWRunParamConf。指令信息详见指令字段描述。
采用网关运行参数指令每次可以Gate的一个参数项，如果需要设置多个参数项，多次下发。如可通过运行参数指令设置Unit的log是否同步转发给Host。

5.1.6 Gate对Host屏幕控制的处理
![img](.\bmp\B5.1.6.png)

5.1.7 Host下发固件升级到Gate处理
Host可通过[UpdateFireware](#_固件升级（UpdateFirmware）)指令通知充电设备进行固件升级，Gate将收到的升级指令信息转发给Update升级服务，由Update升级服务判断充电桩当前是否具备升级条件，通过Update升级服务将判断结果通知给Gate，Gate收到Update升级服务通知后立刻同步应答Host升级确认。
Update升级服务判断如果具备升级条件，Upddate升级服务立刻启动升级流程。固件升级完成后，Host可通过[UpGateInfo](#_网关信息上传（UpGateInfo）)信息得知升级后的软件版本信息。
![img](.\bmp\B5.1.7.png)
Update升级服务在升级过程将会把升级过程状态发送给Gate，Gate通过[UpMessage](#_主动上行消息（UpMessage）)消息将升级状态推送给Host。

5.1.8 Gate主动上行消息
Gate主动向Host转发单元模块Unit的数据有两条指令，一条是实时主动上行消息[UpMessage](#_主动上行消息（UpMessage）)，一条是主动上行离线消息[UpOfflineMessage](#_主动上行离线消息（UpOfflineMessage）)。
[UpMessage](#_主动上行消息（UpMessage）)用于实时转发Unit的消息到Host，一般用于在线信息同步转发。该指令消息每次只允许转发一条Unit到Host信息。Gate收到Host的应答后，需更新指令的业务类型判断是否需要转发Unit。
[UpOfflineMessage](#_主动上行离线消息（UpOfflineMessage）)用于将Gate处理离线状态（Gate与Host通讯异常）缓存的实时数据（遥测、遥信等）和log日志数据（Gate配置为同步转发）主动上报给Host。该指令每次可以转发多条Unit到Host的信息。Gate收到Host的应答后，无需转发到Unit单元模块。

5.1.9 远程排毒参数控制
充电桩作为电动汽车充电的基础设施，当自身出现时，充电桩应具备自修复能力，能够在用户无感的前提下提供正常充电功能。做最大努力使充电桩能够7*24不间断提供充电服务。
排毒机制只在用户场景启用，不在测试场景开启，避免实际问题逃过。如果未开启排毒机制，需上报是否启用状态桩给运维平台。
排毒原则：用户无感，不影响车主充电需求；
排毒周期：1天，1周，1月，默认：1周，可远程修改配置；
排毒时机：空闲状态，时间可远程修改， 时机可个根据具体场景经验数据修改；
家桩&专用场站： 上午排毒，默认时间 9:00
商桩&公开场站： 深夜排毒，默认时间 3:00
排毒通道：整桩主动硬件复位          { 5寸交流桩功率板无硬件复位信号}
排毒输出：每次主动复位排毒不产生复位异常记录，而只产生一次排毒事件；
排毒参数的设定和获取详见**《6.2.5 读写网关运行参数RWRunParam》**
5.2 单元模块UNIT通讯建立处理

5.2.1 通讯建立
参考“[GATE网关与UNIT单元模块之间的通信约定](#_GATE网关与UNIT单元模块之间的通信约定)”。
单元模块作为客户端，在与GATE网关通信前需先进行签到，若单元模块有子模块，子模块也需要通过单元模块发送签到消息进行签到，单元模块签到成功后才能进行通信，子模块在单元模块签到成功之后，通过单元模块发送子模块签到消息进行签到，通信断开重连之后单元模块和子模块都需重新签到。
考虑到向前兼容，如果是主节点，GATE就采用报文格式的源地址作为节点ID；如果是子节点，签到信息里面需包括子节点ID,便于Gate上传至Host填充节点id。源地址保持用主节点的节点ID，无论签到的是主节点，还是子节点。
![img](.\bmp\B5.2.1.png)

5.2.2 通讯维护
单元模块应该每n秒（定值设置）发送一次心跳包，统计心跳包应答情况。
GATE网关应该统计连续N秒（定值设置）接收心跳包情况，如果收到0包，则应该主动断开与该单元模块的通讯连接（Socket）。同时取消该单元模块的签到状态。
![img](.\bmp\B5.2.2.png)
单元模块丢失M次（定值设置）心跳后，应该主动断开与GATE网关的通讯连接（Socket）。
![img](.\bmp\B5.2.2-2.png)

5.2.3 系统时间
GATE网关应当在每次单元模块“签到”时候发送一次“时钟同步”到该单元模块，同时按照1小时为周期重复发送到每个已经“签到”的单元模块。
建立的报文不上传给监控平台Host*，只用于维护UNIT和Gate之间的通信链路状态。**

5.2.4 应答不支持业务类型
当GATE网关或者单元模块接收到一条消息，但不支持其中的业务类型，应当应答不支持该业务类型。如果接收到的一条消息中有多个不支持的业务类型，该应答不支持该业务类型数据包中可同时包含多个不支持的业务类型。

5.2.5 多包数据传输业务类型
当单元模块或Gate需要发送一个大数据包时候，由于网络发送长度和内存大小限制需要分包发送。在接收完每个分包后，再把它们组成一个业务数据包而后解析。
对于数据长度大于2048字节的数据，单元模块和Gate之间采用[多包数据传输方式传输](#_多包数据传输接口)。
目前，多包数据传输可用于传输故障录波数据和ECU\CCU固件升级数据。

5.2.6 通用JSON数据传输
[通用Json数据传输接口](#_通用JSON数据传输接口)（业务类型：0x0180，0x0181，0x0182，0x0183）主要用于Unit与Host之间传输边长或数据字段经常更改的数据信息。该组通讯接口包括上行通讯（0x0180,0x0181）和下行通讯（0x0182,0x0183）。
上行通讯是由Unit发起通讯，包括请求和应答两个指令，每次成对出现。
下行通讯是由Host发起通讯，包括请求和应答两个指令，每次成对出现。
通用json数据传输接口传输的数据区需根据json内部的code对应解析，字段dataObj是个可选字段，应根据实际业务进行json字符串解析。[code与DataObj定义详见附录H。](#_附录H_通用JSON数据传输定义)
5.3 单元模块UNIT传输控制处理

5.3.1 远程复位
单元模块接收到远程复位包后，发送应答包，同时停止发送其它数据包到GATE网关，并在3秒后重启。
![img](.\bmp\B5.3.1.png)

5.3.2 设置工作模式
GATE网关应该在所有充电枪停止充电后才能发送该设置命令。
![img](.\bmp\B5.3.2.png)
单元模块应该在不充电的状态下才能执行工作模式转变。
![img](.\bmp\B5.3.2-2.png)

5.4 单元模块UNIT的控制台
单元模块应支持控制台（命令行）交互功能，需要支持常用基础命令，同时支持根据单元模块自身情况定义的自定义命令。
命令行解析，将输入字符分解成命令和参数，它们以空格区分开。其命令执行格式如下：
cmd [arg1] […]
控制台设置登陆密码，防止在单元模块上非法执行命令。
单元模块自己判断当前是否可执行命令。如工作模式等的要求。
![img](.\bmp\B5.4.png)

5.4.1 Host发送控制台命令到单元模块
Host通过“主动下行消息”组包，数据包括“控制台命令请求”。然后发送给Gate，Gate接收并转发到单元模块。

5.4.2 单元模块应答控制台命令到Host
单元模块通过“控制台命令响应”发送应答包给Gate，然后Gate按照“主动上行消息”组包并发送给Host。

5.5 定值参数
Host云平台可以设置和查询单元模块的定值参数。如ECU的过压欠压告警值等。
每个定值都有被设置的时间窗口，如与充电有关的定值应该在停止充电后才能被设置。
单元模块应该在定值被允许设置的时间窗口才正确响应该设置定值命令。

5.6 记录数据上传
记录数据主要包括5类：启动完成记录,停止完成记录,事件记录，故障/告警记录,故障录波记录。
单元模块上传的每条记录都需要Gate做应答，确保已经可靠送达。上传的数据需根据分类按照时间发生顺序上传给Gate。
![img](.\bmp\B5.6.png)
Gate通过“PushRecord消息”上传记录数据至Host。如果Gate与Host连接断开，待连接恢复后，再将缓存文件中的记录数据补传给Host。
录波数据的定义：是出现故障前后5S的信息的上下文数据，每隔50ms存储一次数据块，数据块数量=10*（1000/50）=200。

5.7 远程升级
GATE网关应该在所有充电枪停止充电后才发送升级文件。
![img](.\bmp\B5.7.png)
单元模块应该在所有充电枪停止充电后才接收升级文件。
![img](.\bmp\B5.7-2.png)
GATE网关应该在所有充电枪停止充电后才发送用于升级作用的复位命令。
单元模块的Bootloader应该在启动时候检查升级文件区中升级文件的版本，并与运行的固件版本比较，升级的版本更新时则立刻启动更新固件。
GATE网关在接收到升级文件，标记文件的目标板和版本号，一起存储。
GATE网关根据“签到”信息判断是否应该给目标板升级。升级流程参考“[升级维护接口](#_升级维护接口)”章节。
第三方大包升级模式本地触发升级或查询最新固件说明：
（1）当为第三方大包升级时，如果需要从充电桩本地触发升级，那么首先需要从远程运维平台获取当桩可升级的最新固件URL,因为每次发布的固件或存储在服务器上的固件url地址不确定的，需要充电桩主动获取URL。
（2）大包升级不需要像原来但模块下载升级一样，和升级服务通讯，获取固件地址；

5.8 单元模块调试Log输出
单元模块log输出功能包括两部分：（1）远程调试log输出参数设置和查询；（2）远程调试log的输出和存储；

5.8.1 远程调试log输出参数的设置和查询
该部分功能主要是用于通过运维平台远程设置和查询 Gate 转发单元模块输出log的等级参数，通过**“输出等级”**参数的设定，Gate决定哪些log信息同步转发到运维平台，哪些信息不转发到运维平台。
输出等级：Fault，warning，info和debug四个等级。
当设置为fault级别输出时，那么Gate只转发Fault级别的log信息；
当设置为warning级别输出时，那么Gate转发Fault和warning级别的log信息；
当设置为info级别输出时，那么Gate转发Fault，warning和info级别的log信息；
当设置为debug级别输出时，那么Gate转发Fault，warning，info和debug级别的log信息；
涉及业务ID: 0x0171,0x72,0x0174,0x0175

5.8.2 远程调试log输出和存储
单元模块根据自身的需要，通过业务类型ID:0x0170推送log到Gate，Gate网关收到单元模块推送的log后，首先不管推送的log信息是哪个级别，首先需要将log存储起来，然后根据运维平台设定的同步转发log等级参数 “输出等级” 进行转发。
GATE网关在整点系统时间时存储一份Log文件，当文件行数大于__待定__行时，重新开启一个新的日志文件。文件命名的规则为“log_SN_AAA_BB_yyyymmdd_n.log”。
SN：SN为充电桩整机的序列号。
AAA：单元模块简称,如CCU,ECU,TMD等；
BB-单元模块节点ID，详见附录节点ID定义
yyyymmdd：日志产生的日志
n：为文件序号，默认重1开始，同一天可能产生多个日志文件。
示例：
存储第一个CCU日志的文件 log_1234567890_CCU_40_20220309_1.log
当日志文件过大后，产生第二个日志文件 log_1234567890_CCU_40_20220309_2.log
依次类推，文件名增加文件需要
注：目前单元模块Log数据包中的“目的地址”固定为Gate网关。

上报实时数据

SECC信息数据在每次CCU开机及启动充电时主动上报；
远程控制
应该在单元模块处于调试模式时才发送调试控制命令。单元模块应该在调试模式时才正确响应调试控制命令。

5.11  ECU特定接口处理
上报实时数据
应该定时上报和关键数据变化时候上报，同时，事件发生和故障告警发生时候也上报一次。周期上报时间周期可通过“传输控制工作参数”设定。
远程控制
应该在单元模块处于调试模式时才发送调试控制命令。单元模块应该在调试模式时才正确响应调试控制命令。
5.12  DTM特定接口处理

5.12.1 远程控制
DTM单元模块主要涉及远程停止充电、远程禁用控制、远程解禁控制、远程复位控制和参数复位控制。
[远程停止充电控制](#_远程停止充电)是用于运维平台特定需要的控制充电枪停止充电的指令通道。
[远程禁用控制](#_远程禁用控制)指令可在运维平台根据运营、运维需要控制充电桩整机或特定充电枪在指定时间范围内禁止使用，该指令不能在充电中启用。
[远程解禁控制](#_远程解禁控制)指令可恢复被远程禁用的充电桩或或特定充电枪解禁。

5.12.2 时区查询和设置
时区查询用于运维平台查询充电桩的时区信息，运维平台下发查询指令到DTM单元模块，返回充电桩当前时区ID、系统时间、夏令时。
时区设置用于运维平台设置充电桩的时区信息，运维平台下发设置指令到DTM单元模块，时区ID参数必须为国际标准时区ID，格式保持完全一致，DTM收到指令后，修改系统时区参数，并通知UI-Apk更新显示

| 序号 | 参数名称     | 字段类型 | 字段长度 | 备注                                                     |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1        | 模块序列号（SN） | ASCII码      | 32Byte       |                                                              |
| 2        | 硬件版本         | BIN码        | 2Byte        | 硬件版本号组成分为：主版本号，次版本号。  示例：硬件版本号为V1.00，主版本号标识为01H，次版本号标识为00H；报文字节发送顺序为01H 00H。 |
| 3        | 软件型号         | ASCII码      | 12Byte       | 示例：“DCC0101”                                              |
| 4        | 软件版本         | BIN码        | 3Byte        | 软件版本号组成分为：主版本号，次版本号和发行版本号。  示例：软件版本号为V1.00.00，主版本号标识为01H，次版本号标识为00H，发行版本号为00H，报文字节发送顺序为01H 00H 00H。 |
| 5        | 工作模式         | BIN码        | 1Byte        | 0表示正常模式；1表示调试模式；其它值无效；                   |
| 6        | IP地址           | BIN码        | 4Byte        | 单元模块所在硬件板的IP地址（日志监控网口）                   |
| 7        | MAC地址          | BIN码        | 6Byte        | 单元模块所在硬件板的MAC地址（日志监控网口）                  |
| 8        | 子节点数量       | BIN码        | 1Byte        | 0表示没有子节点，1表示有一个子节点。示例：ACU有PLC这一个子节点，那么该位为1 |
| 9        | 子节点序号       | BIN码        | 1Byte        | 没有子节点该位一直为0，有子节点该位为子节点序号（子节点排序从1开始排）.示例：当此签到数据包为ACU版本信息时该位为0，PLC版本信息时该位为1 |

独占模式下，第一把枪插枪或预约时其他枪进入禁用状态，只有当第一把枪拔枪后其他枪才变成可用。 | | 4 | maxCurrList | List | 0..4 | 各充电枪充电电流配置列表

充电桩监控运维通讯协议规定了运维平台和充电桩及充电桩内部智能模块之间的通信物理层、数据链路层、交互流程、报文分类、报文格式和内容的定义。本协议主要包括两部分内容：第一部分详细讲述了充电桩与运营平台之间的通信方式、认证鉴权方式和之间的通信消息格式；第二部分详细阐述充电桩内部网关与单元模块通讯交互细节，为远程监控和故障诊断提供底层信息支持。

CCU (充电控制单元): 用于实现与车辆BMS交换，充电机对车辆的输出控制。ECU/dECU (功率控制单元): 用于实现安全充电机的安全保护和功率模块的调整输出。ACU (功率控制单元): 用于实现交流桩的安全保护和电流输出。TCU (计费控制单元): 用于实现计费、刷卡、计量等功能。GATE (监控网关): 充电桩内部网关，连接云平台和内部模块。HOST (运维监控平台): 云端运维监控平台。UNIT (单元模块): 充电桩内部功能模块。
监控网关GATE与运维监控平台HOST之间通过WebSocket协议通信。WebSocket连接URL格式: wss://<host>:<port>/ws/gate/<gate_id>。WebSocket子协议名称: autel.charger.monitor.v2。认证鉴权采用Token-based authentication和证书验证。
请求消息格式包含: msgId (唯一消息ID), msgType (请求类型), timestamp (时间戳), gateId (网关序列号), payload (请求数据)。响应消息格式包含: msgId (原始消息ID), msgType (响应类型), timestamp, code (返回码), message (消息), payload (响应数据)。所有消息使用JSON格式。

监控网关Gate核心功能包括: 1) Gate上报网关信息到Host - 网关状态上报、心跳机制、在线/离线检测; 2) Host下发复位控制命令到Gate - 远程复位能力; 3) Host拉取Gate宿主设备日志处理 - 日志采集请求、日志文件传输; 4) Gate主动上报记录数据到Host - 充电会话记录、错误/告警上报、状态变化; 5) Host设置/获取网关参数到Gate - 配置管理; 6) Gate对Host屏幕控制的处理 - 显示控制命令; 7) Host下发固件升级到Gate处理 - OTA固件升级、版本验证、回滚支持。
单元模块UNIT通讯建立处理: 1) 通讯建立 - 模块注册、能力协商; 2) 通讯维护 - Keepalive机制、连接恢复; 3) 系统时间 - 时间同步、NTP支持; 4) 应答不支持业务类型 - 不支持消息的错误处理; 5) 多包数据传输业务类型 - 大数据传输、包分片; 6) 通用JSON数据传输 - 通用数据交换格式。UNIT传输控制处理包括远程复位和设置工作模式。
通信拓扑结构: 运维监控平台(HOST) 通过WebSocket(WSS)连接监控网关(GATE)。GATE通过内部协议(TCP/UDP)连接各单元模块: CCU(充电控制)、ECU(功率控制)、TCU(计费控制)、ACU(交流控制)。一体机IP地址采用192.168.x.x可配置格式，各模块使用不同默认端口。

text:
Error Code: 5012
描述: 冷却液液位过低故障
判断条件: 检测到液冷系统上报冷却液位过低故障信号时，报冷却液位过低告警
操作员指引: 液位过低，需补充冷却液； 液冷枪线降额充电
远程维修: 指导客户或现场人员打开终端柜门，检查液位，检查接插件是否松脱
现场维修: 打开终端柜门，目视检查液位是否低于3. （1）若液位低于3，请加注冷却液至液位5~6之间。加液后，重启液冷终端 （2）若液位高于3，则液位传感器异常/需更换。 打开终端柜门，目视检查接插件是否松脱，若松脱需重新插好.

判断条件: 当充电枪采集的温度值接近充电枪温度探头短路时，持续5S，报充电枪温度探头短路故障

text:
Error Code: 202F
描述: 直流输出电流过流保护
判断条件: 充电过程中，CCU检测到充电输出电流出现以下情况时，判断为有故障(10s)： 1.车辆最大允许电流<=5A时,充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流150mA； 5A<车辆最大允许电流<=50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流+1.5A； 车辆最大允许电流>50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流的3%； 2.车辆需求电流<=50A时,充电输出电流超出车辆需求电流+2.5A； 车辆需求电流>50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆需求电流的5%。
操作员指引: 过流故障触发车辆充电安全保护策略，暂停充电，并联系售后
远程维修: 通知客户或现场人员确认
现场维修: ①排查是否是某个充电模块问题；②排查是否是CCU采样问题

text:
Error Code: 305C
描述: CCU电压采样与模块输出电压误差告警（误差过大）
判断条件: 正常启动充电后，ECU获取每把枪对应使用模块的输出最大电压，对比检测CCU内侧采样的电压作对比误差告警判断。 1.连续检测60s，误差大于20V告警 2.存在告警中连续60s检测到小于等于15V解除告警
操作员指引: 模块异常，联系后台确认故障原因，确认后排除异常或更换模块
远程维修: 指导客户或现场人员检查充电模块和CCU是否正常工作

描述: 背板NFC通信异常告警

text:
Error Code: 5016
描述: TReturn+/-温度过高告警
判断条件: 检测到Treturn温度大于85℃时，报TReturn+/-温度过高告警
操作员指引: 回液温度过高，液冷枪线降额充电
远程维修: 指导客户或现场人员检查 1. 进出风口是否被遮挡 2. 风扇和泵是否运转正常 3. 停机4小时以上且未充电状态，Treturn温度是否仍大于环温10℃以上
现场维修: 检查 1. 检查进出风口是否被遮挡 2. 检查风扇和泵是否运转正常 3. 停机4小时以上且未充电状态，检查Treturn温度是否仍大于环温10℃以上

text:
Error Code: 205D
描述: 涓流时间过长
判断条件: 排除空载等状况后，充电机输出电流在涓流电流范围内持续5min，充电机主动停止充电 1、SOC大于95%以上，电流小于定值持续一定时间
操作员指引: 少部分车辆的电池技术能力不足，长时间的小电流充电占用电力资源的同时易造成起火风险。安全考虑，需联系技术支持
远程维修: 无需处理
现场维修: 确认桩端无故障，检查车辆是否是SOC大于95%，如果是则无异常。

text:
Error Code: 205B
描述: 充电枪温度探头开路
判断条件: 当充电枪采集的温度值接近充电枪温度探头开路时，持续5S，报充电枪温度探头开路故障
操作员指引: 过温故障可能由软件误报和硬件故障造成，先进行软件复位，如果再次出现相同故障报警，联系客服指导现场操作
远程维修: 指导客户或现场人员检查车和桩端充电接口是否有异物、磨损或烧蚀
现场维修: 现场用测温枪测试实际温度，如果并无明显过温，推测温度采样问题，考虑温度传感器和CCU；如果确实过温，检查车和桩端充电接口是否有异物、磨损或烧蚀

text:
Error Code: 202F
描述: 直流输出电流过流保护
判断条件: 充电过程中，CCU检测到充电输出电流出现以下情况时，判断为有故障(10s)： 1.车辆最大允许电流<=5A时,充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流150mA； 5A<车辆最大允许电流<=50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流+1.5A； 车辆最大允许电流>50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆最大允许电流的3%； 2.车辆需求电流<=50A时,充电输出电流超出车辆需求电流+2.5A； 车辆需求电流>50A时，充电输出电流超出车辆需求电流的5%。
操作员指引: 过流故障触发车辆充电安全保护策略，暂停充电，并联系售后
远程维修: 通知客户或现场人员确认
现场维修: ①排查是否是某个充电模块问题；②排查是否是CCU采样问题

描述: 涓流时间过长

text:
Error Code: 205B
描述: 充电枪温度探头开路
判断条件: 当充电枪采集的温度值接近充电枪温度探头开路时，持续5S，报充电枪温度探头开路故障
操作员指引: 过温故障可能由软件误报和硬件故障造成，先进行软件复位，如果再次出现相同故障报警，联系客服指导现场操作

现场维修: 如果万用表测量到正常电压，桩采集到不正常电压，则更换充电桩（single charger）或更换ACU（dual charger）

text:
Error Code: 400B
Description: Ground fault
描述: 接地故障
判断条件: 零线N对PE线电压大于70V
Condition: The voltage between neutral line N and PE wire is greater than 70V.
操作员指引: 可能为客户电网进线接地异常 请检查交流进线的地线是否连接正常，尝试重新接地线。
远程维修: 1. 核对交流进线安装方式是否与安装手册相同，重点检查PE接线远程维修指引应该是检查日志，查看日志中N-PE的电压值，如果大于70V，则需要进行现场排查。
现场维修: 1. 核对交流进线安装方式是否与安装手册相同 2. 使用万用表检查PE线与配电箱PE线导通情况，如果导通则为正常。 3. 如果仍然有问题，single charger则更换充电桩，如果是dual charger，则更换ACU

text:
Error Code: 400D
Description: Overtemperature
描述: 温度过高故障
判断条件: 桩内环境或元器件温度≥105℃时，报过温故障
Condition: An over-temperature fault is reported when the internal environment or component temperature of the charger reaches or exceeds 105 °C.
操作员指引: 检查充电桩周边环境温度，确保通风良好，无太阳直射
远程维修: 检查出现问题时是否为充电过程出现，如果是空闲阶段出现，且其他温度传感器均没有过温，则可能为内部传感器故障
现场维修: 1. 指导客户断电后重新上电，观察现象是否消失 2. 检查软件版本是否正常，更新为最新版本 3.如故障仍然存在： single charger需更换充电桩 Dual charger请更换ACU

text:
Error Code: 400E
Description: DC leakage current
描述: 直流漏电流故障
判断条件: 充电过程中，发生直流漏电流故障
Condition: A DC leakage current fault occurs during charging.
操作员指引: 充电回路异常，有漏电流，可能为桩内部故障或枪线、车辆故障 使用其他车辆充电，如果没有漏电流的故障，则是车的问题，如果问题仍然存在，联系Autel技术支持解决。
远程维修: 1. 断电后重新上电，观察现象是否消失 2. 检查软件版本是否正常，更新为最新版本 3.更换其他车辆观察是否可充电，其他车辆不可充电，则为桩或充电枪故障
现场维修: 1. 断电后重新上电，观察现象是否消失 2. 检查软件版本是否正常，更新为最新版本 3.更换其他车辆观察是否可充电，其他车辆不可充电，则为桩或充电枪故障

text:
Error Code: 400F
Description: CP abnormal
描述: CP异常故障
判断条件: CP_6V电压：2~7.2V； CP_9V电压：7.6V~10.2V； CP_12V电压：11~13V； 当CP电压不在该范围内时，报CP异常故障
Condition: CP_3V Voltage: 2.5~4V; CP_6V Voltage: 4.85~7V; CP_9V Voltage: 7.9V~10V; CP_12V Voltage: 11~12.6V. When the CP voltage is not within this range, a CP abnormal fault will be reported.

text:
Error Code: 4017
Description: PME fault
描述: PME故障
判断条件: 当接三相电时，零线N对PE电压大于等于70V，报PME故障； 当接单相电时，L对N电压大于等于262.2V或者小于等于207V时，报PME故障。
Condition: For three-phase power, a PME fault is reported when the voltage between Neutral (N) and Protective Earth (PE) is ≥ 70V. For single-phase power, a PME fault is reported when the voltage between Line (L) and Neutral (N) is ≥ 262.2V or ≤ 207V.
操作员指引: 可能为客户电网电压异常 检查电网电压是否在正常范围内，如果电网电压正常，则联系Autel技术支持解决
远程维修: 1. 远程查看桩所采集到的电压是否在正常工作范围之内 2. 使用万用表测量电网电压是否在正常范围内
现场维修: 如果万用表测量到正常电压，桩采集到不正常电压，则更换充电桩（single charger）或更换ACU（dual charger）

Description: AC leakage current
描述: 交流漏电流故障
判断条件: 充电过程中，发生交流漏电流故障

text:
Error Code: 401E
Description: Output ground fault
描述: 输出接地故障
判断条件: 当输出端接地异常时，CP电压会变动，当CP电压不在范围内时，判断为输出接地异常
Condition: When the output is abnormally grounded, the CP voltage will fluctuate. If the CP voltage is out of range, it is considered an output grounding fault.
操作员指引: 该信号为车辆与桩对接信号，可能为桩故障或车辆故障，如车辆可以在其他桩正常充电则需要检查充电桩 更换其他车辆充电，如果故障仍然存在，则联系Autel技术支持解决。
远程维修: 1. 使用万用表检查CP-PE电压在空闲状态下是否为11~12.6V区间内，如果该电压不正常，则充电桩或者枪线异常 2.更换其他车辆观察是否可充电，其他车辆不可充电，则为桩故障
现场维修: 1. 使用万用表检查CP-PE电压在空闲状态下是否为11~12.6V区间内，如果该电压不正常，则充电桩或者枪线异常，更换枪线 2.更换其他车辆观察是否可充电，其他车辆不可充电，则为桩故障，如果是single Charger则更换充电桩，如果是Dual charger则更换ACU

描述: 强磁故障
判断条件: 任意方向强磁超过0.5mT报故障，停止充电

现场维修: 如重启后状态无法恢复，需更换充电桩

text:
DFMEA RPN评分标准

DFMEA RPN评分标准
1、FMEA严重评价准则
后果 评定准则：后果的严重度 严重度
无警告的严重危害 这是一种非常严重的失效形式，它是在没有任何失效预兆的情况下影响到人身安全或不符合政府的法规 10
有警告的严重危害 这是一种非常严重的失效形式，是在具有失效预兆的前提下所发生的，影响到人身安全或不符合政府的法规 9
很高 产品不能正常工作/运行（丧失基本功能） 8
高 产品可工作/运行，但消费者可以发现性能明显下降，顾客非常不满意 7
中等 产品可工作/运行，但舒适性/方便性等性能严重下降，甚至缺失，顾客非常不满意 6
低 产品可工作/运行，但舒适性/方便性等性能有所下降，顾客有些不满意 5
很低 外观性等轻微不良，大多数顾客（75%以下）能感觉到有缺陷 4
轻微 外观性等轻微不良，部分有辨识能力的顾客（50%以下）能感觉到有缺陷 3
很轻微 外观性等轻微不良，少有的有辨识能力的顾客（25%以下）能感觉到有缺陷 2
无 没有可识别的后果 1
2、FMEA频度评价准则
失效发生可能性 可能的失效 频度
很高：持续性发生 ≥100000PPM（不良率10%） 10
50000PPM（不良率5%） 9
高：经常性失效 20000PPM（不良率2%） 8
10000PPM（不良率1%） 7
中等：偶然性失效 5000PPM（不良率0.5%） 6
2000PPM（不良率0.2%） 5
1000PPM（不良率0.1%） 4
低：相对很少发生 500PPM（不良率0.05%） 3
100PPM（不良率0.01%） 2
极低：失效不太可能发生 10PPM（不良率0.001%） 1
3、FMEA探测度评价准则
可探测性 准则：设计控制可能探测出来的可能性 侦测度
绝对不肯定 设计控制将不能和/或不可能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型，或根本没有设计控制 10
很极少 设计控制只有很极少的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 9
极少 设计控制只有极少的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 8
很少 设计控制只有很少的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 7
少 设计控制有较少的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 6
中等 设计控制有中等的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 5
中上 设计控制有中上多的机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 4
多 设计控制有较多机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 3
很多 设计控制有很多机会能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 2
几乎肯定 设计控制几乎肯定能找到潜在的起因/激励及后续的失效模型 1
